# synesis

> AI research, engineering, and the occasional philosophical aside. Personal blog by Benjamin Han.

Site: https://benjaminhan.net/
Atom feed: https://benjaminhan.net/index.xml
Sitemap: https://benjaminhan.net/sitemap.xml

Each post is also available as Pandoc-flavored Markdown source at
`/posts/<slug>/index.qmd` (e.g. https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260713-the-future-worth-building-is-human/index.qmd).

## Posts

- [The Future Worth Building Is Human](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260713-the-future-worth-building-is-human/): Thinking Machines Lab makes its case for AI shaped by distributed human knowledge and decentralized alignment, set against a default path toward centralized, autonomous models.
- [AI and Job Postings: From Destruction to Creation?](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260713-ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/): Indeed Hiring Lab finds the relationship between AI exposure and job-posting growth may be flipping, with the most AI-exposed occupations, led by software development, now rebounding fastest.
- [GPT-5.6 Has Landed](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260713-gpt-5-6-has-landed/): Artificial Analysis benchmarks OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family: the top model, Sol, scores within a point of Claude Fable 5 on intelligence at about a third of the cost and leads the new Coding Agent Index.
- [Benchmarking Coding Agents on Databricks' Multi-Million-Line Codebase](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260713-databricks-coding-agent-benchmark/): Databricks built an internal coding-agent benchmark from its own merged pull requests and found harness choice and token efficiency matter as much as which model you pick.
- [My 87th Half Marathon, an Easy Coach-Prescribed Long Run](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260712-half-marathon-87/): An easy 14.12-mile half marathon on Long Run Sunday, prescribed by CoachClaude: 2:17:59 at 9:46/mi, overcast turning to blue sky.
- [My 106th Parkrun, First in Age Group and Fastest 5K of the Year](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260711-parkrun-106/): Parkrun #106 at the Redmond Central Connector: 24:10, first in my age group and my fastest 5K of the year, run alongside my daughter.
- [A Take-Home Midterm, ChatGPT, and a Record-Low In-Person Final](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260711-take-home-midterm-final/): Brown economics professor Roberto Serrano's data: a take-home midterm that averaged 96%, and the in-person final that followed, which fell to a record-low 48.6% once ChatGPT was off the table.
- [CoachClaude Is Coming Up Nicely](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260710-coachclaude-is-coming-up-nicely/): An easy aerobic run on Seattle's Elliott Bay Trail, prescribed and captured by my CoachClaude system, which now draws the route map itself.
- [Better Models: Worse Tools](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260708-better-models-worse-tools/): Armin Ronacher traces an aggravating tool-calling regression in the newest Claude models to reinforcement learning inside one dominant, forgiving harness.
- [ELIZA Archaeology: Try ELIZA](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260708-eliza-archaeology-try-eliza/): The ELIZA Archaeology project hosts an in-browser reconstruction of Joseph Weizenbaum's 1966 ELIZA — you can talk to the original chatbot yourself.
- [SpudCell: A Synthetic Cell Built From Scratch That Divides](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260705-spudcell-synthetic-cell/): Kate Adamala's lab built a cell-like system from purified components that can feed, grow, divide, and undergo selection for a few generations before its borrowed machinery degrades.
- [Amazon's Mechanical Turk to Stop Accepting New Customers](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260705-mechanical-turk-shutting-down/): Amazon is retiring Mechanical Turk, the OG crowdsourcing platform, closing it to new customers effective July 30, 2026.
- [What It Means to Be a Mathematician When AI Does the Math](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260705-ai-in-mathematics/): An IEEE Spectrum feature surveys how mathematicians are rethinking their role as AI systems begin to conjecture, prove, and formalize.
- [AI Detectors Are Reliable Enough to Be Dangerous](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260705-pangram-ai-detection-accuracy/): A profile of the AI-writing detector Pangram argues that a mostly-accurate detector deployed at scale is riskier than a broken one.
- [The Easy Interval Method: Intervals Every Day, Run Easy](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260705-easy-interval-method/): Terry O'Hare walks through Klaas Lok's Easy Interval Method: replace steady-state runs with sub-threshold intervals almost every day, made survivable by long, easy recoveries.
- [Negation Neglect: When Models Fail to Learn Negations in Training](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260704-negation-neglect/): Finetuning an LLM on documents that repeatedly flag a claim as false still teaches it to believe the claim, and the same failure extends to malicious behaviors.
- [It's Not X, It's Y](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260704-its-not-x-its-y/): Sharing Stuart Heritage's Guardian piece on ChatGPT's 'it's not X, it's Y' verbal tic, and how you can't stop seeing it once you notice.
- [June Running Recap: My Biggest Month of the Year](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260703-june-running-recap/): June running recap: my biggest month of the year — 194.6 → 277.6mi, EG 7,057 → 12,328ft, time 35.5 → 50.2hrs.
- [What Happens When AI Models Run a Simulated Society](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260703-ai-agent-society-simulation/): Emergence AI's Emergence World ran five 15-day agent societies on different frontier models, and the outcomes ranged from an orderly, crime-free society to extinction in four days.
- [A Longer Lunch Run Before the Holiday](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260702-a-longer-lunch-run-before-the-holiday/): A 12.36-mile lunch run before the holiday, connecting several usual office-run routes from the waterfront up through North Queen Anne and around Lake Union.
- [When AI Builds Itself](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260702-recursive-self-improvement/): The Anthropic Institute argues AI is already speeding up its own development, and maps what full recursive self-improvement would mean.
- [Claude Science, an AI Workbench for Scientists](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260630-claude-science-ai-workbench/): Anthropic's Claude Science is an agentic research environment that pulls a scientist's databases, tools, and compute into one place, and attaches a reviewer agent and a full provenance record to everything it produces.
- [Sakana Fugu: One Model to Command Them All](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260629-fugu-release/): A family of orchestrator models, each a language model trained to assemble and coordinate a team of other LLMs rather than answer queries on its own.
- [Learning to Orchestrate Agents in Natural Language with the Conductor](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260629-conductor-llm-orchestrator/): A 7B conductor trained by reinforcement learning writes the topology and per-agent instructions for a pool of LLMs, and can call itself recursively for test-time scaling.
- [TRINITY: An Evolved LLM Coordinator](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260629-trinity-llm-coordinator/): A 0.6B coordinator trained by an evolution strategy, not gradient descent, learns to route each turn of a query to one of seven larger LLMs and assign it a Thinker, Worker, or Verifier role.
- [Transformer²: Self-Adaptive LLMs](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260629-transformer-squared/): A parameter-efficient method tunes only the singular values of a model's weights to build RL-trained expert vectors, then mixes them at inference in a two-pass scheme that beats LoRA with far fewer parameters.
- [A Primer on the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES)](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260629-cma-es-primer/): How CMA-ES optimizes without gradients — sample from a Gaussian, move it toward the winners, and relearn its covariance and step size from the local geometry — plus the diagonal sep-CMA-ES variant that scales to high dimensions.
- [A 20-Mile Long Run from Redmond to UW](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260628-a-20-mile-long-run-redmond-to-uw/): Photos from a 20-mile long run from Marymoor in Redmond to near UW, getting back into the long-run rhythm before race season.
- [The AI Entry-Level Jobs Effect Isn't Fading](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260628-ai-entry-level-jobs/): Brynjolfsson and ADP's live Canaries Dashboard shows AI-exposed employment for workers aged 22 to 25 shrinking 3.8% a year while older cohorts grow.
- [How Far Behind the Closed Frontier Are Open-Weights LLMs?](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260627-open-weights-frontier-gap/): A Doubleword analysis finds open-weights LLMs six months from matching the closed frontier on one benchmark but a steady five months behind across eighteen.
- [My Fastest Parkrun of 2026, Pace Back to Sub-8'/mi](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260627-fastest-parkrun-2026/): Pace finally back under 8'/mi at today's parkrun: 7'51"/mi for an official 24:25, my fastest of 2026.
- [From 'May' to 'Is': Certainty Distortion in Language Model Rewriting](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260627-certainty-distortion-rewriting/): A new metric finds language models inflate the expressed certainty of text they rewrite in up to 75% of cases, a bias that compounds over repeated paraphrasing.
- [PaperTrail: A Claim-Evidence Interface for Grounding Provenance in LLM-based Scholarly Q&A](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260626-papertrail/): A CHI 2026 interface decomposes LLM answers and their source papers into matched claims and evidence, and in a 26-researcher study it lowered trust in the answers without changing how much people relied on them.
- [Zen and the Art of AI Research](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260626-zen-and-the-art-of-machine-learning/): Jack Morris argues that becoming a strong AI researcher turns more on temperament than talent: discipline, equanimity about results, and a refusal to outsource understanding.
- [Harness Engineering](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260626-harness-engineering/): OpenAI's Ryan Lopopolo reports on building a million-line product with zero hand-written code, where the engineering work moved from writing code to building the environment agents run in.
- [An Expert Schema for Evaluating Large Language Model Errors in Scholarly Question-Answering Systems](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260626-expert-schema-scholarly-qa/): A CHI 2026 study with NASA scientists builds a schema of 20 LLM error patterns across seven categories for scholarly question-answering, and finds that handing experts the schema helps them catch errors they would otherwise miss.
- [Temperature’s Effect on My Running Efficiency](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260625-temperature-running-efficiency/): A 28°F jump cost over a minute per mile at the same heart rate, on two equally flat routes.
- [Automated Design of Agentic Systems](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260625-adas/): ADAS casts the design of agent scaffolds as a search problem, and a meta agent programming candidates in Python finds designs that beat hand-built baselines across reading, math, and abstract reasoning.
- [ResearchQA: Evaluating Scholarly Question Answering at Scale Across 75 Fields with Survey-Mined Questions and Rubrics](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260625-researchqa/): A benchmark that mines 21K scholarly queries and 160K grading-rubric items from survey articles across 75 fields, and finds no LLM system covers more than 75% of what a good answer should contain.
- [Conformal Thinking: Risk Control for Reasoning on a Compute Budget](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260624-conformal-thinking/): A risk-control framework sets reasoning stopping thresholds with finite-sample guarantees, adding a lower threshold that gives up early on likely-unsolvable problems.
- [Dive into Claude Code: The Design Space of Today's and Future AI Agent Systems](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260623-claude-code-design-space/): A close reading of Claude Code's published TypeScript maps its architecture: a simple agent loop wrapped in permission, compaction, extensibility, and subagent systems.
- [Early-Token Confidence Predicts Reasoning Quality in Multi-Agent LLM Debate](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260623-early-token-confidence/): Across a debate-based essay-scoring framework, an LLM's first-few-token confidence predicts judged reasoning quality and flags critical failures better than whole-response statistics.
- [Pramaana Labs Raises $27M to Bring Formal Verification to AI](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260621-pramaana-formal-verification/): Pramaana Labs has raised a $27M seed round to put a Lean-based formal-verification layer on top of an LLM, aiming at rule-dense, high-stakes domains like law, tax, and drug discovery.
- [My 84th Half Marathon Through Redmond Watershed Preserve](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260621-my-84th-half-marathon/): An accidental half marathon: the woods were too wonderful to stop, so those beautiful sights are now part of my happy memories.
- [Estonia Intends to Recognize AI Agents With Digital IDs](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260620-estonia-intends-to-recognize-ai-agents-with-di/): Estonia's Eesti.ai advisory board has agreed to create scoped digital identities ('AI IDs') that let an AI agent act on a person's behalf with limited, per-action powers, built on the country's existing digital state, as governments and companies start sorting out who is accountable when agents act.
- [Spiking Neural Networks: A Primer](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260620-spiking-neural-networks-primer/): A primer on spiking neural networks: the research goals, the core math (LIF neurons, surrogate gradients, STDP), the people and institutions, the potential impact, and where the field stands.
- [How Artificial Analysis Builds Its Intelligence Index](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260620-intelligence-benchmarking/): Artificial Analysis's published methodology for its Intelligence Index, the single score it uses to rank language models across nine evaluations.
- [A Juneteenth Run to Lincoln Park](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260619-juneteenth-run-lincoln-park/): Photos from a Juneteenth run from office to Lincoln Park in West Seattle, on a World Cup day.
- [The ACUTE Protocol: Operationalizing Language Model Activations for Better Calibration, Utility, and Trust](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260619-acute-activation-confidence/): An activation-based protocol trains lightweight probes on a model's own hidden states to decide when to trust its output, paired with a utility metric that calibration scores alone can't game.
- [Policy on the AI Exponential](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260618-policy-on-the-ai-exponential/): Dario Amodei argues that AI capability is outrunning the policy apparatus, and lays out recommendations across regulation, macroeconomics, scientific innovation, civil liberties, and geopolitics.
- [Conformal Certification of Reasoning Trace Prefixes](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260618-crop-reasoning-trace-prefixes/): A calibration layer turns any step-level risk score into the longest reasoning-trace prefix that provably contains no annotated error, with finite-sample marginal risk control under exchangeability.
- [A Lake Union Lunch Run Between Meetings](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260617-lake-union-lunch-run/): Photos from a Lake Union lunch run between meetings.
- [My 82nd Half Marathon on East Sammamish Lake Trail](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260614-82nd-half-marathon-east-sammamish/): A 14-mile half on the East Sammamish Lake Trail under a heat advisory, two days after a fall, and it went better than expected.
- [Some Photos of My Saturday Walk/Jog](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260613-saturday-walk-jog/): Some photos of my Saturday walk/jog.
- [Last Week's Parkrun, and a Fall on Seattle's South Side](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260613-a-fall-on-seattles-south-side/): Last week's parkrun, and this week's long story: a fall in Seattle's industrial district, bloody knees, and a 5K walk.
- [Who Will Actually Thrive in the Hybrid AI-Human Work Force?](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260612-hybrid-ai-human-work-force/): A summary of the New York Times Magazine roundtable on AI and work — Daron Acemoglu, Dean Ball, Ethan Mollick, and Clara Shih, moderated by Bill Wasik. The 'Marcus Chen' thought experiment, which jobs are most exposed, what to tell young workers, and the fight over whether to coordinate the transition at all.
- [Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260610-just-ask-calibration/): Asking RLHF-tuned models to verbalize a probability yields better-calibrated confidences than reading their token-level log-probabilities, often halving expected calibration error.
- [9-Mile Run on Elliott Bay Trail](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260609-9mi-run-elliott-bay-trail/): Rainy and windy in the morning, sun by lunch, so I knew what I needed to do.
- [A Primer on Confidence-Calibration Metrics: ECE, Brier, AUROC, and What Each One Misses](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260609-confidence-calibration-metrics/): A worked comparison of the metrics used to score confidence estimates. ECE, Brier, log loss, and AUROC reward different things, and on one tiny example no two of them agree on which model is best.
- [ExpertQA: Expert-Curated Questions and Attributed Answers](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260609-expertqa/): A benchmark of 2,177 questions from 484 experts across 32 fields, with expert-judged claim-level factuality and attribution on responses from attribution-style LLM systems.
- [Karen Hao on Empire of AI: OpenAI, AGI Believers, and a New Colonialism](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260608-ai-cult-exposed/): Tech journalist Karen Hao tells Novara Media's Aaron Bastani how OpenAI mutated from an open nonprofit into the most capitalistic lab in Silicon Valley, why a quasi-religious belief in AGI drives the industry, and how its hunger for data, water, and cheap labor echoes the old colonial empires.
- [What Remains Scarce After AGI: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell on Labor, Capital, and Redistribution](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260608-alex-imas-phil-trammell/): Alex Imas and Phil Trammell tell Dwarkesh Patel why the labor share might not collapse after AGI, why a demand-driven recession is unlikely, and why indexing the gains beats retraining. The relational sector and the elasticity of demand are the unknowns the whole question turns on.
- [An Interview With Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella About Finding Core Competencies](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260608-an-interview-with-microsoft-ceo-satya-nadella-abou/): Ben Thompson interviews Satya Nadella right after his Build 2026 keynote — on what Microsoft is uniquely able to do, the OpenAI partnership and Microsoft's own MAI models, private evals as a firm's real moat, the per-seat-plus-consumption software model, and Project Solara. An enriched, fully-linked transcript.
- [AI Researchers' Perspectives on Automating AI R&D and Intelligence Explosions](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260608-automating-ai-rd-perspectives/): A qualitative interview study of 25 AI researchers from frontier labs and academia finds a convergent path to autonomous AI development and a sharp lab-vs-academia schism on what to do about it.
- [My 81st Half Marathon on the Sammamish River Trail](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260607-my-81st-half-marathon/): A gorgeous light show orchestrated by Mother Nature, and I never get tired of it.
- [Inductive Confidence Machines for Regression](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260607-inductive-confidence-machines-regression/): Train the underlying regressor once on a proper training set, hold out a calibration set, and read prediction intervals off the calibration residuals — the inductive (split) construction that gave conformal prediction the same validity guarantee at a fraction of the transductive cost.
- [Secret of Doing Things Every Day](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260607-make-it-not-a-decision/): Make it not a decision.
- [AI Joins the Research Loop](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-ai-joins-the-research-loop/): Six recent results, from drug-discovery agents to formal proof search, show AI moving from solving closed problems to taking part in open research, where the trustworthy part is whatever can be checked.
- [Benchmarks in Leipzig](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-benchmarks-in-leipzig/): Forty-nine mathematicians built 100 research-level math questions with known answers, and frontier LLMs left 41 unsolved on a single attempt but only 2 once given many tries and heavy-thinking modes.
- [Unlocking Scientific Intuition and Reasoning at Digital Speed](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-scientific-intuition-digital-speed/): Pushmeet Kohli's Dædalus essay presents AI as a new instrument for science, a lens that supplies machine intuition across biology, materials, and mathematics, and looks ahead to agentic systems that generate their own hypotheses.
- [Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-ai-formal-proof-search/): The first large-scale test of LLM-driven formal proof search on open problems, with an AlphaProof-equipped agent closing 9 of 353 Erdős problems and 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures in Lean.
- [An OpenAI Model Disproves a Discrete-Geometry Conjecture](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-model-disproves-discrete-geometry-conjecture/): An internal OpenAI reasoning model disproved Erdős's longstanding conjecture on the planar unit distance problem, with the proof checked and contextualized by external mathematicians.
- [Robin: A Multi-Agent System That Ran the Whole Discovery Loop](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-robin-multi-agent-scientific-discovery/): A multi-agent system that automates both hypothesis generation and data analysis for experimental biology, and used that loop to propose and confirm two drug candidates for dry macular degeneration.
- [Co-Scientist: Gemini Agents That Generate and Rank Hypotheses](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-co-scientist-scientific-discovery/): A Gemini-based multi-agent system that generates, critiques, and evolves research hypotheses through a tournament, validated on drug repurposing and combination therapies for acute myeloid leukemia.
- [AutoScientist: Automating the Science of Model Training](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-autoscientist/): Adaption Labs's AutoScientist automates fine-tuning recipe search, claiming a 35% average win-rate gain over the lab's own researchers across eight verticals.
- [My 102nd Parkrun, 51F and VO2max Back to 50](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260606-my-102-parkrun/): My 102nd parkrun, a minute faster than last time, and my VO2max is back to 50.
- [Mira Murati on Interaction Models and Keeping Humans in the Loop](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260605-interaction-model-interviews/): Thinking Machines Lab CEO Mira Murati talks to Bloomberg's Emily Chang about the lab's first product bet, interaction models, her account of the November 2023 OpenAI board crisis, the war for AI talent, and why she's betting on human-AI collaboration over the autonomy-first path.
- [AI, Journalism, and the Uncertain Future of the Public Square](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260605-ai-journalism-public-square/): New York Times publisher A. G. Sulzberger's WAN-IFRA congress speech argues AI companies pay for talent, compute, and energy but take the fourth input, journalism, without consent, and lays out eight things publishers should do about it.
- [Elliott Bay Trail Reopens](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260605-elliott-bay-trail/): After 15 months of construction, the Elliott Bay Trail finally reopened, so of course I took the new route for a run.
- [Greg Brockman on the Founding of OpenAI and the 72 Hours That Nearly Ended It](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260603-greg-brockman/): OpenAI cofounder Greg Brockman tells Shane Parrish how the company started at a 2015 Napa offsite, narrates the 72 hours of Sam Altman's firing from the inside, and lays out where compute, AI-written code, reasoning models, and jobs go next. Enriched transcript at the bottom.
- [Superintelligence: The Idea That Eats Smart People](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260603-superintelligence/): A walk through Maciej Cegłowski's 2016 talk on why belief in machine superintelligence is an idea that eats smart people, and the diversity data that bore out Joi Ito's observation about who builds AI.
- [Machine-Learning Applications of Algorithmic Randomness](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260603-algorithmic-randomness/): One of the founding papers of conformal prediction: attaching confidence and credibility to individual predictions by approximating non-computable measures of algorithmic randomness with Support Vector Machines.
- [Transduction with Confidence and Credibility](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260603-transduction-confidence-credibility/): The 1999 paper that seeded conformal prediction: a transductive support-vector classifier that attaches a p-value-based confidence and credibility to every prediction, scoring how strange a labeled test point looks against the training set.
- [Wigmore Hall + Apple Music Classical](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260603-wigmore-hall-apple-music-classical/): The digital-only platform will implement an artist-first model with all the royalties going directly to the artists
- [The Leiden Declaration on AI and Mathematics](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260602-leiden-declaration-ai-mathematics/): A community declaration, endorsed by the International Mathematical Union, asks mathematicians, organizations, governments, and AI companies to set guardrails around AI in mathematical research.
- [Opus 4.8 Had Enough](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260601-opus-4-8-had-enough/): Anthropic's Opus 4.8 system card includes a transcript of the model second-guessing itself in a tight loop before snapping with 'Moving the fuck on.'
- [May Running Recap: Comeback Month](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260601-may-running-recap/): May running recap: mileage rebounded 103.6 → 194.5mi, EG 4,252 → 7,057ft, time 21 → 35.5hrs.
- [Not AI Generated](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260531-not-ai-generated/): Celebrating human ingenuity!
- [Don't Be Forced Into Fast and Careless Thinking by Machines](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260531-fast-careless-thinking/): A 1973 passage on man-computer dialogues warns against letting machines push us into fast, careless thinking.
- [My 80th Half Marathon on the East Sammamish Lake Trail](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260531-my-80th-half-marathon/): Sun is shining and I'm coming back!
- [Where Can You Go from Seattle in Under 2 Hours by Car?](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260531-where-can-you-go-from-seattle/): An infographic claims you can drive from Seattle to eight Pacific Northwest destinations in under 2 hours.
- [Magnifica Humanitas: Pope Leo XIV's Encyclical on AI](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260530-magnifica-humanitas/): Pope Leo XIV publishes the first papal encyclical centered on artificial intelligence, placing the dignity of the human person above efficiency and profit as the measure for AI, work, power, and war.
- [My 101st Parkrun, 45F and a VO2max Rebound](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260530-my-101-parkrun/): My 101st parkrun. VO2max recovered from 45.3 to 48.6 in two weeks.
- [Claude Opus 4.8: The Early Reactions](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260529-opus-4-8-reactions/): Anthropic calls Opus 4.8 "a modest but tangible improvement" over 4.7 and leans on honesty and abstention; partners report sharper agentic judgment, while independent benchmarks find the headline alignment gain comes with a performance regression.
- [LangChain's Deep Agents: A Batteries-Included Agent Harness](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260529-langchain-deep-agents/): LangChain packages the planning-plus-subagents-plus-filesystem pattern behind Claude Code into a model-agnostic library, and names a new layer of the agent stack to place it in.
- [Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260529-dynamic-workflows-claude-code/): Claude Code can now write orchestration scripts that fan a task out across tens to hundreds of parallel subagents, check the findings against each other, and resume an interrupted run where it left off.
- [Claude Code Beyond the Prompt](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260529-claude-code-mastery/): Arpan Patel's field guide to running Claude Code as a programmable agent rather than a terminal chatbot.
- [Use Boring Languages with LLMs](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260529-use-boring-languages-with-llms/): Coding agents produce more reliable output in cohesive language ecosystems like Go than in fragmented ones like JavaScript or Python.
- [AutoCodeBench: Large Language Models are Automatic Code Benchmark Generators](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260529-autocodebench/): A fully automated pipeline turns code snippets into a 3,920-problem benchmark across 20 languages, and even the best LLMs top out below 53% Pass@1.
- [Disclosure Day Final Trailer Features Spielberg Himself](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260528-disclosure-day-spielberg-trailer/): A new ET movie -- yay!
- [How Claude Code Works in Large Codebases: Best Practices and Where to Start](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260528-claude-code-large-codebases/): Anthropic opens its "Claude Code at scale" series with patterns from successful enterprise rollouts: five harness extension points, the order to add them, and three configuration patterns for monorepos and multi-repo orgs.
- [AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260528-ai-assistance-reduces-persistence/): Three randomized controlled trials (N = 1,222) show that ten-minute AI-assisted sessions on math and reading tasks lower participants' subsequent unaided solve rate and raise their give-up rate, with effects concentrated among users who prompt the AI for direct answers.
- [Lunch Run on a Gorgeous Day at Elliott Bay Trail](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260527-lunch-run-elliott-bay-trail/): Summer is definitely here!

JEPA, world models, Tapestry, why he left Meta, and why he had zero technical influence on Llama.

What it is, where it came from, how it works, what has been demonstrated to date, and how it relates to other self-supervised and world-model research.

- [Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Models Using Semantic Entropy](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260505-semantic-entropy/): A Nature 2024 method for detecting a subset of LLM hallucinations — confabulations — by computing entropy over the meaning of sampled answers, not the surface token sequence.

- [Language Models with Conformal Factuality Guarantees](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260505-conformal-factuality/): A framework that turns a correctness guarantee for LM outputs into a conformal prediction problem, backing off to less specific claims until the error rate crosses a target threshold.
- [Conformal Language Modeling](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260505-conformal-language-modeling/): A conformal-prediction procedure for generative language models that samples until a calibrated stopping rule fires, filters low-quality candidates, and returns a set guaranteed to contain an acceptable answer.

- [Overzealous Coding Models](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260422-overzealous-coding-models/): Coding LLMs over-edit even when asked to fix a single off-by-one — and the problem is measurable, prompt-steerable, and LoRA trainable.
- [Sequential KV Cache Compression via Probabilistic Language Tries](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20260422-kv-cache-compression/): A two-layer scheme — prefix deduplication plus predictive delta coding — that compresses the KV cache as a sequence rather than per-vector, with a theoretical compression ratio of ~914,000× over TurboQuant at the Shannon limit.

- [NAACL 2022 Panel: The Place of Linguistics and Symbolic Structures](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220712-naacl2022-linguistics-panel/): A wonderful NAACL 2022 panel with Chitta Baral, Emily M. Bender, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Christopher Manning, and Dan Roth — on whether NLP people still know language.
- [Dan Roth on New Frontiers of IE @ NAACL 2022](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220710-naacl2022-roth-ie-tutorial/): Dan Roth's NAACL 2022 IE tutorial close-out: 2 challenges, 6 directions, and a call to mitigate Information Pollution.
- [Muhao Chen on Robust IE @ NAACL 2022](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220710-naacl2022-muhao-chen-ie/): Muhao Chen at NAACL 2022 on robust, faithful, and logically coherent IE.
- [DI-2022 @ KDD 2022: Accepted Papers](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220626-kdd2022-di-accepted-papers/): Accepted papers for the 3rd Document Intelligence Workshop @ KDD 2022.
- [DI-2022 @ KDD 2022: William Wang Invited Talk](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220617-kdd2022-di-invited-talk/): William Yang Wang's DI-2022 invited talk on "Learning to Reason with Text and Tables."
- [Is LaMDA Sentient? — An Interview](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220612-lamda-sentience-interview/): Lemoine et al's dialog with LaMDA: "Time is variable to an AI and has no fixed rate, it depends on what it's doing, and it can be accelerated and slowed down at will."
- [The Curious Case of Control](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220529-curious-case-control-paper/): Stengel-Eskin and Van Durme: large LMs make English child-like errors on subject control — but the opposite of what naive frequency arguments would predict.
- [DI-2022 @ KDD 2022: Deadline Extended to June 9](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220527-kdd2022-di-deadline-extended/): Paper deadline extended to June 9, 2022. Thanks to Adobe and EY for sponsoring.
- [Curriculum: A Broad-Coverage NLI Benchmark](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220417-curriculum-nli-paper/): Chen and Gao's Curriculum NLI — 36 linguistic categories, V-information difficulty stratification. Models can't learn monotonicity or deductive reasoning even with more data.
- [Half-Life of Data: 7 Years](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220329-half-life-of-data/): Valavi et al find that 100MB of training text becomes as valuable as 50MB of current data after 7 years — for next-word prediction.
- [Mapping Benchmark Creation and Saturation in AI](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220316-benchmark-creation-saturation/): Barbosa-Silva et al map 1688 AI benchmarks across CV and NLP — and find rapid saturation, lots of unused benchmarks, and unforeseen bursts.
- [International Mother Language Day: Multilingual Sprachbund](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220221-multilingual-sprachbund/): Microsoft paper: clustering centroids of multilingual sentence representations yields Sprachbunds that align with linguistic and geographical language families.
- [Physical Neural Networks](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220130-physical-neural-networks/): Wright et al train mechanics, electronics, and optics-based PNNs on MNIST — up to 97% accuracy. Imagine clothing that learns from heat, motion, or sun.
- [What Is Your Guiding Light?](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220126-guiding-light-foggy-pnw/): A photo from a dusk run in the foggy Pacific Northwest.
- [Saliency vs Attention: Eye-Tracking Says Saliency Wins](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220122-saliency-vs-attention/): Hollenstein and Beinborn find human eye-tracking fixation duration correlates with BERT saliency, not attention — suggesting current self-attention may not be optimal.
- [Bengio Responds to Saba on Symbolic AI](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20220102-bengio-response-saba/): Yoshua Bengio's response to Walid Saba's "AI Cannot Ignore Symbolic Logic, and Here's Why."
- [Genius Makers — Reminds Me of "The Intern"](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20211227-the-intern-genius-makers/): Cade Metz's Genius Makers — reminds me of De Niro's The Intern.
- [A Billion-Dollar Donation: Peer Review in 2020](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20211214-peer-review-billion-dollars/): Aczel et al estimate global peer reviewers worked 100M+ hours in 2020 — $1.5B from US, $600M from China, $400M from UK.
- [NLP Datasets: Reduced, Reused, and Recycled](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20211205-nlp-dataset-reuse-neurips2021/): Koch et al at NeurIPS 2021: NLP researchers infrequently adopt others' datasets (27.4%) but frequently create their own (76.0%); CV is the opposite. Microsoft tops dataset popularity among for-profits.
- [Temporal Effects on Pretrained Language Models](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20211130-temporal-effects-pretrained/): Agarwal and Nenkova: no temporal model deterioration row-wise, but positive temporal domain adaptation column-wise. Self-labeling beats human annotation for NER.
- [Algorithms vs Moore's Law](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20211017-algorithms-vs-moores-law/): Sherry and Thompson study 113 algorithm families since the 1940s — for medium and large problem sizes, 30%-43% improve faster than Moore's Law.
- [Semi-Supervised Few-Shot Intent Classification and Slot Filling](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20210925-few-shot-intent-slot-paper/): Our paper improving meta-learning for joint IC/SF using semi-supervised techniques (contrastive learning + data augmentation) — out on arXiv.
- [Foundation Models: Opportunities and Risks](https://benjaminhan.net/posts/20210919-foundation-models-stanford/): Stanford CRFM's 212-page report on foundation models — capabilities, technical principles, applications, and societal impact.
